title: Architecture & Standards: API, Coding, Infra, Model-Serving, Observability, Performance, ADRs
author: Maya Patel
body:
Overview

This page consolidates Redwood Inference's architecture and engineering standards across API design, coding practices, infrastructure, model-serving, observability, performance, and the ADR (Architecture Decision Record) process. The goal is to provide deterministic guidance teams can apply when designing services that will be hosted on Redwood (hosted, dedicated, or private) so that surfaced telemetry, reliability targets, and developer ergonomics remain consistent across the company.

Scope

- Applies to all new services and substantial refactors of existing services in the Redwood runtime, control plane, and customer-facing APIs.
- Includes microservices, serverless functions, model-serving components, SDKs, and infrastructure code (Terraform/CloudFormation).
- Excludes one-off experiment prototypes that are not intended for production; prototypes should still follow the ADR and rollout checklist if promoted to production.

1) API Standards

Purpose: Ensure consistent, versioned, and discoverable APIs (internal and external) that are safe for clients to depend on.

Design principles:
- Use RESTful resources for CRUD-style endpoints; prefer RPC-style endpoints only for complex multi-stage operations (e.g., streaming generation sessions).
- API base path must include a service name and semantic version: /api/v1/{service}/{resource}. Do not use date-based versions in the path.
- Backwards-compatible changes: additive fields, new endpoints, new query parameters. Non-backwards-compatible changes require a new major version (v2).
- Use consistent paging (cursor-based) for list endpoints.
- Rate limiting: default per-tenant quota + burst window. Responses must include X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset headers for public/hosted endpoints.

Error model (JSON):
- Standard error response: { "error": { "code": "string", "message": "human readable", "details": [ "optional array of strings" ] } }
- Use HTTP status codes: 4xx for client errors (400/401/403/404/429), 5xx for server errors. Prefer 503 with Retry-After for service-wide throttling.

Authentication and authorization:
- External APIs: OAuth2 bearer tokens for human flows, API keys for machine-to-machine where appropriate.
- Internal services: mTLS + short-lived service tokens issued by the control plane.
- Sensitive scopes must be documented in the API spec and require an owner to approve onboarding.

API documentation and spec:
- Every public or internal API must publish an OpenAPI 3.0 spec in the repository at /openapi.yaml and a generated HTML spec published to the docs site.
- Breaking changes must include an ADR and migration guide.

2) Coding Standards

Purpose: Maintain readable, testable, and secure codebases across languages used at Redwood.

General rules (all languages):
- Follow language idioms; prefer idiomatic constructs over clever micro-optimizations.
- Mandatory code reviews with at least one reviewer from outside the immediate team for public APIs or infra changes.
- Unit test coverage: aim for >=80% on logic-heavy modules; critical modules (auth, billing, model-runtime) must include integration tests in CI.
- CI checks must include linting, type checks (where available), and security scans (Snyk/Trivy for containers).
- Avoid long-lived secrets in code; use the secrets manager (SecretsVault) and reference by env var.

Language-specific guidance:
- Python: follow PEP8, use black for formatting and mypy for static typing. Pipenv/Poetry preferred for dependency management.
- Go: use gofmt, vet, and add a module-level go:generate where codegen is used. Prefer context.Context propagation for cancellation and instrumenting traces.
- TypeScript/Node: enable strict mode in tsconfig.json, prefer functional decomposition and use ESLint with recommended rules.

Dependency management:
- Dependabot or equivalent automated updates required for third-party libs; major upgrades require a PR with an ADR if they change behavior of core services.

3) Infrastructure Standards

Purpose: Ensure consistent, auditable, and reproducible infrastructure across cloud accounts and on-prem packaging.

IaC and modules:
- Use Terraform as the canonical IaC for cloud-managed infra. A central module registry exists at infra-modules.redwood.dev; all modules used by teams should source canonical modules rather than copy/paste templates.
- Module naming convention: rg_<product>_<component> (e.g., rg_runtime_gpu_pool).
- State: remote state locked in our central backend (Terraform Cloud or S3 with Dynamo lock). No local state in PRs.

Accounts & networking:
- VPC design: shared services in a hub VPC, tenant workloads in spoke VPCs. Use VPC endpoints for internal services where possible.
- Default network ACL: deny-by-default, allow minimum required ingress.

Secrets and keys:
- Use the company SecretsVault (KMS-backed) for secrets. Key rotation policy: rotate symmetric keys every 90 days; rotate asymmetric and KMS keys annually or on suspicion of compromise.

Deployment and releases:
- All prod deployments must be automated via CI/CD pipelines with immutability guarantees (immutable AMIs or container image digests).
- Feature flags must be used for risky UI/behavioral rollouts; flags live in the LaunchDarkly account namespaced by team.

4) Model-serving Standards

Purpose: Provide consistent and production-safe practices when onboarding and serving models across Redwood's hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.

Model packaging & metadata:
- Every model bundle must include a manifest.json with fields: model_id, architecture, tokenizer, request_schema, quantization_profile, recommended_batch_sizes, owners, and license. The manifest must be human-readable and validated in CI.

Versioning and rollouts:
- Model versions are immutable artifacts. Use semantic versioning for non-breaking changes to metadata; breaking behavior changes require a new major model id (e.g., t5-small-v2 -> t5-small-v3).
- Canary serving: rollouts must progress from canary (1% traffic) -> ramp (10%) -> 50% -> 100% with automated quality gates (latency, correctness on golden prompts).

Quantization and compatibility:
- Recommended quantization profiles should be stored in quantization-profiles/ in the model repo and must specify supported hardware (A100, H100, T4), dtype (INT8/FP16), and expected accuracy delta vs. baseline.
- Runtime must validate KV cache compatibility across pinned model revisions.

Routing and fallbacks:
- Smart routing policy names: latency-first, cost-first, region-preferred. Routing configuration must be declared in route-config.yaml per service.
- Define fallbacks for capacity failures: fallback to compatible model variant (e.g., fp16 -> int8) or to lower-cost region; fallback policies must preserve security and data locality constraints.

5) Observability Standards

Purpose: Instrumentation baseline that enables fast troubleshooting, capacity planning, and SLA verification.

Metrics:
- All production services must expose Prometheus-compatible metrics and publish to the central metrics pipeline. Metric naming convention: redwood_<service>_<resource>_<metric> (e.g., redwood_runtime_v2_inference_latency_ms).
- Required metrics: request_count, request_errors, request_duration_seconds_bucket (histogram), queue_depth, batch_size_distribution (summary/gauge).
- Cardinality rules: avoid high-cardinality labels on frequently scraped metrics. Acceptable cardinality for tenant_id: only sampled or as an aggregate dimension, not as a label on high-frequency metrics.

Logging:
- Structured JSON logs with fields: timestamp, level, service, trace_id, span_id, request_id, tenant_id (when applicable), message, and extra. PII must never be logged.
- Error logs should include stack traces and a minimal reproduction context.

Tracing and distributed context:
- All services must propagate trace context (W3C Trace Context). Traces should include span attributes for model_id, model_version, batch_size, and hardware_type.

Dashboards and alerts:
- Each service must publish a service overview dashboard (latency p50/p95/p99, error rate, throughput, capacity utilization).
- Alerting: page on SLO breach (see SLOs below) or sustained error-rate spike > 5% for 5 minutes. Pager duty runbooks must be linked from the alert.

6) Performance Standards

Purpose: Define measurable targets and benchmarking methodology for inference and control-plane services.

SLOs and targets (default for interactive generation endpoints):
- Latency SLOs: p95 < 150 ms, p99 < 400 ms for short-context generation endpoints (<= 512 tokens) on Dedicated/hosted tier; private deployments may vary based on on-prem hardware (documented in customer config).
- Availability SLO: 99.95% monthly for Dedicated and Hosted control-plane endpoints.
- Throughput targets: per-GPU throughput guidance is documented in the model-performance catalog and should be validated during model onboarding.

Benchmarking and perf-suite:
- Use the canonical benchmarking harness (eng-serving-runtime/benchmarking-and-perf-suite) to validate latency and throughput at multiple batch sizes and sequence-length distributions.
- Bench runs must include: cold-start latency, warm KV-cache latency, and sustained QPS to detect head-of-line and queuing effects.

Batching & cache guidance:
- Default batching policy: adaptive batching with max_batch_size recommended by the model manifest. Aim to keep mean batch size > 1.5 under typical workload to amortize kernel overheads.
- Cache: enable prefix and KV caching for repeated prompt families; cache TTL default 30 minutes for ephemeral prompts, configurable per-route.

7) ADR (Architecture Decision Record) Process

Purpose: Capture rationale for architecture-level decisions and make them discoverable.

When to create an ADR:
- Any decision that changes service boundaries, API contract, security posture, infra topology, or cross-team dependency must have an ADR.

ADR template (file per ADR in docs/adr):
- Title
- Status: proposed | accepted | deprecated | superseded
- Context (problem statement)
- Decision (what we decided)
- Consequences (operational/dev impact)
- Owners
- Date

ADR lifecycle:
1. Draft ADR in the team repo under docs/adr/xxxx-title.md.
2. Request reviewers (including architecture guild) and indicate reviewers in the ADR frontmatter.
3. After review, publish the ADR to Confluence and link it from related code repos.
4. If an ADR is later superseded, create a new ADR referencing the previous one and mark the previous as superseded.

Decision review board:
- For cross-cutting or high-risk ADRs, escalate to the Architecture Review Board (representatives from infra, serving-runtime, security, and product) for approval.

8) Rollout and Release Checklist (must be completed before 100% traffic cutover)

- [ ] ADR recorded for any breaking or large-scope change.
- [ ] OpenAPI spec added/updated and a generated client smoke-tested.
- [ ] Canary deployment and monitoring configured (automated canary checks for latency and correctness).
- [ ] Load test results attached to the release PR (bench harness artifacts).
- [ ] SLO dashboards and alerts created/updated.
- [ ] Security review completed for new scopes/data flows.
- [ ] Owner and on-call rotation documented in team wiki.

9) Ownership and Contacts

- Standards owners: Architecture Guild (architecture-standards@redwood.dev) - maintain this page and coordinate cross-team reviews.
- Infra modules: eng-infra.
- Model onboarding & quantization profiles: applied-ml-and-evals/model-onboarding.
- Observability: eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts.

10) References and examples

- Example OpenAPI error schema: /templates/api/error-schema.json
- Terraform module registry: https://infra-modules.redwood.dev
- Quantization profile examples: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles/sample-profiles.yaml
- ADR canonical directory: /confluence/architecture-and-standards/adr-index

Appendix: Example API snippet (OpenAPI-like pseudo YAML)

openapi: 3.0.0
info:
  title: Redwood Runtime Inference API
  version: v1
paths:
  /api/v1/runtime/generate:
    post:
      summary: Generate text from a model
      requestBody:
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              $ref: '#/components/schemas/GenerateRequest'
      responses:
        '200':
          description: successful generation
        '429':
          description: rate limit exceeded

Components:
  schemas:
    GenerateRequest:
      type: object
      properties:
        model_id:
          type: string
        input:
          type: string
        max_tokens:
          type: integer

Feedback and updates

If you have proposed changes to these standards, open a PR against the architecture-standards repo and tag the Architecture Guild in the PR. Significant updates will be communicated in the monthly architecture guild sync and published to the Confluence page with a changelog entry.
